transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapur (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Mark Chen (Tessera Procurement), Aisha Rahman (Tessera Security), Diego Alvarez (Tessera Eng)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We're joined by Priya, our systems engineer, and Samir on onboarding. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark Chen: Good thanks. We've got the procurement packet open. Want to walk through MSA and DPA main asks.
[00:12] Priya Kapur: Great, we'll cover contract items and then jump to the technical bits - SLAs, pilot sizing, and onboarding.
[00:20] Aisha Rahman: Quick note from security side - main blockers are SOC 2 attestation, KMS/HSM support, and data residency controls. We'll need evidence and answers in the vendor questionnaire.
[00:32] Jordan Lee: Totally understood. We can provide our SOC2 report and ISO cert links. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and HSM integrations for private deployments. We'll include the docs.
[00:45] Diego Alvarez: When you say private deployments - does that mean VPC peering or on-prem appliance? What's the timeline?
[00:51] Priya Kapur: Two options. Hosted Dedicated capacity (reserved pools in our managed infra) with VPC peering and private subnets; or Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem where the control plane is customer-managed. On-prem requires more lead time - typically 6-8 weeks for packaging and network validation.
[01:12] Mark Chen: For our procurement timeline, finance needs predictable pricing and SLAs before vendor signoff. What do your SLA tiers look like?
[01:20] Jordan Lee: We have Hosted (standard) with best-effort and uptime backing for the API, and Dedicated with SLA-backed latency and availability. For enterprise onboarding we can commit to 99.9% monthly availability on Dedicated and have escalation matrices. We'll share the SLA appendix.
[01:33] Aisha Rahman: Is there an option for higher SLA, like 99.95, with super-critical routing?
[01:38] Samir Patel: Yes, higher SLA tiers are available as an add-on with dedicated hot-standby capacity and multi-region failover - that would be in the enterprise pack. Pricing increases because of reserved capacity.
[01:49] Diego Alvarez: Pricing - curious about burst capacity. If we run periodic spikes, do you auto-scale or is it part of the contract?
[01:56] Priya Kapur: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity windows. For strict cost predictability we recommend reserved commit plus a defined burst allowance. We'll put sample numbers based on your projected token volumes.
[02:08] Mark Chen: On the MSA/DPA redlines: legal flagged data deletion clauses and liability caps. Also DPA needs to specify subprocessor list and data residency. Can you provide the subprocessor list and agree to EU data residency?
[02:20] Jordan Lee: Subprocessor list is available; we'll provide the latest. For EU residency we can pin data at rest in EU regions for Private and Dedicated; hosted standard may replicate for performance, but we can negotiate residency for your account.
[02:32] Aisha Rahman: Encryption - at rest and in transit, and key separation. We need to know where keys are stored.
[02:38] Priya Kapur: We support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS keys; keys never leave your cloud tenant for private deployments. For hosted, we offer a BYOK flow via KMS integration. We'll document exact flows.
[02:48] [02:50] Jordan Lee: If that's helpful we can share a redline-ready MSA with annotations that address these common asks.
[02:55] Mark Chen: Yes please. Also finance asked for an approval path for pilot pricing - we typically need a 60-day evaluation with locked pilot pricing.
[03:03] Jordan Lee: We can do a 30- to 60-day pilot with locked pricing for the pilot period. We'll send a pilot agreement addendum.
[03:12] Diego Alvarez: For the pilot, what telemetry/logs do we get? We need per-route latency, token usage, and per-request IDs for tracing.
[03:21] Priya Kapur: You'll get request-level logs, per-route dashboards, token-cost breakdowns, traces for retries and fallback, and KV cache hit metrics. We also expose sampling of model outputs for quality checks.
[03:33] Aisha Rahman: Audit logs retention? Our policy requires 1 year of audit logs.
[03:38] Samir Patel: Default retention is 90 days; extended retention packages are available for 1 year or longer as an add-on. We'll put options in the pricing sheet.
[03:48] [04:00] Mark Chen: About insurance and indemnity - we need cyber insurance limits and a mutual indemnification section. Can you confirm carrier limits?
[04:08] Jordan Lee: We carry an industry-standard cyber liability policy; I'll get exact numbers from legal and include them. Indemnities are in the MSA but we can discuss any specific carve-outs you need.
[04:20] Diego Alvarez: Technical deep dive question - latency targets for 2k token chats on Dedicated in eu-west-1.
[04:26] Priya Kapur: For a model like LlamaLarge (example), median tail p95 token latency is in the 60-120ms per-token range on Dedicated with optimized batching; end-to-end for 2k tokens depends on streaming vs full response. We'll provide verified benchmark numbers for the pilot config.
[04:44] Mark Chen: Competitors: CloudGiant offered an always-on node but at double price; ModelHost had different quantization that affected responses. We're trying to justify Redwood choice to execs.
[04:58] Jordan Lee: Understood - we'll include comparison bullets and cost math to make the exec case.
[05:05] [10:20] (discussion continues, some cross talk)
[10:25] Aisha Rahman: About DPA - processor/subprocessor obligations; can Redwood accept standard EU DPA with our amendments around breach notification windows (24 hours)?
[10:35] Jordan Lee: We generally accept 72-hour notification windows but will escalate if we can commit to faster for critical incidents; we'll check with legal if 24-hour is acceptable for your tier.
[10:46] Mark Chen: The procurement team needs to see a sample SLA performance report monthly - is that possible?
[10:52] Samir Patel: Yes we provide monthly SLA reports with uptime, incident summaries, and per-route latency histograms. We'll also include runbooks for incident response.
[11:05] Diego Alvarez: One of our compliance controls requires evidence of SOC2 Type II controls around change management. Where can we get that?
[11:13] Priya Kapur: We can provide the SOC2 Type II report under NDA. We'll send a link to the compliance bundle and provide an inventory of controls mapping.
[11:24] Mark Chen: Will you be able to support SAML SSO for our console?
[11:28] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support SAML and OIDC. We'll include a setup guide and SAML metadata for your IdP.
[11:36] [15:00] (customer asks about onboarding timeline and roles)
[15:05] Samir Patel: Typical onboarding for a Dedicated pilot is 2-4 weeks: account provisioning, VPC peering, pilot config, and benchmark run. Private/on-prem is longer. We can compress if you provide network & security resources quickly.
[15:20] Diego Alvarez: We have a constrained network window on May 12-14; can you work within that?
[15:25] Priya Kapur: We'll aim for provisioning before that window or align pilot start after. We'll capture that as a dependency in the onboarding checklist.
[15:35] Mark Chen: Are there any standard exclusions in the MSA around model outputs? We need responsibility language.
[15:41] Jordan Lee: We have clauses around content usage and customer responsibility for prompts/outputs. We'll highlight those sections and propose language that aligns with your legal team.
[15:50] Aisha Rahman: Is there a pen-test/third-party attestation we can request?
[15:54] Samir Patel: We undergo annual third-party pen tests; we can share the summary and coordinate a scope if you require additional testing for your account.
[16:05] [20:10] (brief pause, then pricing specifics)
[20:12] Jordan Lee: On pricing, here's the typical structure: baseline per-token for hosted; reserved monthly commit for Dedicated; add-on for ingress/egress, extended log retention, and higher SLA tiers. For pilot we'll propose a capped usage price with a one-time onboarding fee.
[20:30] Mark Chen: Finance will want a clear comparison: current vendor costs vs Redwood committed. We can share our token estimates.
[20:36] Jordan Lee: Please send token estimates; we'll build a cost model showing per-token cost, expected savings from prefix caching and batching, and pilot pricing.
[21:00] Diego Alvarez: For integration - does Redwood provide SDKs or internal gateways for routing to the right model?
[21:06] Priya Kapur: We provide REST and SDKs, plus routing rules for model variants, and function-calling support. We'll share example code for streaming and retry logic.
[21:22] Mark Chen: On governance, we need RBAC for console and API keys per-team.
[21:27] Samir Patel: RBAC, team-level keys, and audit trails are supported. We'll document roles and provisioning APIs.
[21:40] [30:00] (mid-call recap)
[30:05] Jordan Lee: Quick recap: we'll send a redline MSA and DPA, SOC2/ISO docs under NDA, pilot pricing and sample SLA appendix, onboarding checklist, and a benchmark runbook. Anything else to add?
[30:18] Aisha Rahman: Please include the subprocessor list and pen-test summary.
[30:22] Mark Chen: And the pilot agreement with locked pricing for 60 days.
[30:26] Jordan Lee: Got it. We'll target sending those items by the dates we discussed.
[30:33] Diego Alvarez: One technical ask - include model determinism/quality regression tests we can run during pilot.
[30:39] Priya Kapur: We'll include evaluation prompts and an auto-eval harness template.
[30:44] [40:00] (questions from procurement about signoffs)
[40:05] Mark Chen: Our procurement needs a single point of contact from your side for vendor paperwork.
[40:10] Jordan Lee: I'll be primary contact for legal and pricing; Samir will handle onboarding and security comms; Priya for technical.
[40:18] Mark Chen: If legal pushes back on indemnity, who should they reach out to?
[40:22] Jordan Lee: Send legal redlines to me and I'll loop in our legal counsel; we typically resolve via a short review cycle.
[40:30] [46:00] (closing items)
[46:05] Jordan Lee: Final next steps recap: Jordan sends redline MSA + pricing by 2026-05-05; Priya runs pilot benchmark and shares runbook by 2026-05-08; Samir shares onboarding checklist by 2026-05-06; Mark to return vendor questionnaire by 2026-05-07. We'll schedule an exec sign-off call the week of 2026-05-11.
[46:30] Aisha Rahman: Noted. We'll review the docs and loop in legal.
[46:35] Mark Chen: Appreciate the quick turnaround.
[46:40] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a Loom + attachments.
[46:46] (meeting ends)

- Jordan: Send redline MSA, DPA, pricing spreadsheet (due 2026-05-05)
